paper_title: EvoUndo: Recoverability-Constrained Self-Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: LLM agents increasingly modify their own prompts, tools, middleware, resources, and execution harnesses at runtime. Such self-evolution can improve capability, but a successful mutation may leave persistent effects that cannot be safely reversed in states different from the one in which it was created. We introduce EvoUndo, a framework for representing, synthesizing, diagnosing, and independently verifying recoverability of model-generated self-modifications across counterfactual states. Across 600 unseen one-shot self-evolution tasks, we identify 197 capability-improving mutations that fail recoverability verification. Under the original recovery representation, conventional repair strategies recover 0/197 of these natural failures. Deterministic oracle analysis recovers 48/197 under the original recovery language L0, while the extended recovery calculus increases empirical oracle recovery to 191/197. A protocol-locked 2x2 grounding-by-expressivity intervention then separates two bottlenecks: exact state-address grounding increases successful recovery from 0/48 to 38/48 (79.2%) when the original language is sufficient, while extending the recovery language enables recovery on 142/143 (99.3%) failures in the oracle-defined S1 stratum. On the primary gpt-oss-120b backbone, adding exact-address diagnostics to the richer language reduces recovery to 133/143 (93.0%); a Qwen3.8-27B replication preserves the grounding and expressivity effects but not this negative interaction, indicating that the latter is model-dependent. These results indicate that reliable agent self-evolution requires co-designing verification, state grounding, witness semantics, and recovery-language expressivity rather than relying on iterative prompting alone.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: LLM agents are increasingly becoming mutable systems. Beyond selecting discrete actions, modern agents can modify prompts, install or remove tools, change middleware, alter configurations, allocate resources, register event listeners, and reconfigure their execution harnesses at runtime (Yin et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2026b; Lin et al., 2026). These capabilities create path toward selfevolving agent harnesses: systems that autonomously adapt their execution environment to novel tasks and failure modes. Most self-improvement procedures naturally optimize the forward effect of modification: given harness state and candidate mutation m, candidate is favored whenever it improves task objective, J(m(H)) > J(H). However, forward improvement is insufficient for long-lived autonomous systems. successful mutation may overwrite configuration values, reorder middleware chains, shadow existing tools, create temporary files, or leak background resources. If that mutation later becomes obsolete, causes regression, or conflicts with subsequent updates, simply applying static inverse operation may fail to restore the prior state. Crucially, the correct recovery procedure is often state-dependent: restoring observational equivalence requires information that existed in the pre-mutation state. 1 This motivates fundamental requirement for autonomous self-evolution: capability-improving mutations must also be robustly recoverable. After applying mutation to state s, the system must be able to utilize pre-mutation state evidence to restore state observationally equivalent to s. Furthermore, this property must hold not merely in the nominal state used during construction, but across counterfactual states in which the mutation may operate. We formalize and investigate this challenge: How should an autonomous agent search for capability-improving harness mutations when robust recoverability is an explicit invariant of the search space? We introduce EvoUndo, framework for recoverability-constrained self-evolution. EvoUndo provides framework for representing, synthesizing, diagnosing, and independently verifying recoverability of model-generated self-modifications. Candidates are executed across counterfactual harness states and admitted only when the recovered states satisfy typed observational equivalence with their corresponding pre-states. Recovery failure is treated as an actionable defect to diagnose and repair before mutation is persistently admitted. central insight of this work is that recoverability is relational: whether mutation is recoverable depends jointly on the state distribution, witness capture semantics, observational contract, and expressivity of the recovery language. On 120 deliberately corrupted but recoverable mutations, verifier-guided typed diagnosis repairs 114/120 (95.0%) cases at budget four, compared with 4/120 (3.3%) under independent regeneration. In sharp contrast, across 600 unseen one-shot self-evolution tasks, 197 capability-positive mutations fail recovery verification, and conventional verifier-guided repair recovers 0/197 under the original recovery representation. zero-generation solvability audit reveals that only 48/197 natural failures are recoverable by the deterministic oracle under the original language L0, whereas an extended language L1 raises empirical oracle recoverability to 191/197. protocol-locked 2 2 grounding-by-expressivity factorial separates these failure modes: exact state-address grounding raises recovery from 0/48 to 38/48 (79.2%) when L0 is sufficient, while L1 unlocks recovery on 142/143 (99.3%) failures in the oracle-defined S1 stratum. On gpt-oss-120b, adding exact-address diagnosis on top of L1 reduces recovery to 133/143 (93.0%), while cross-model replication shows this secondary interaction is model-dependent. Contributions. 1. We formalize recoverability-constrained self-evolution and introduce EvoUndo, coupling harness mutations with witness capture, counterfactual verification, typed diagnosis, and closed-loop recovery synthesis. 2. We establish natural failure benchmark from 600 self-evolution tasks, identifying 197 capability-positive recovery failures where standard iterative repair achieves 0/197 success under the base recovery representation. 3. We decouple natural recovery failures into grounding and expressivity bottlenecks: exactaddress grounding recovers 38/48 (79.2%) failures in S0, while an extended recovery calculus enables recovery on 142/143 (99.3%) failures in S1. 4. We identify backbone-dependent interaction between diagnostic granularity and recoverylanguage capacity: exact-address feedback degrades recovery under L1 on gpt-oss-120b, while this negative interaction does not reproduce on Qwen3.8-27B.

sections.title: 3 EvoUndo
sections.content: 3.1 Candidate Representation and Effect Contracts An EvoUndo candidate is 4-tuple ξ = (m, w, u, Ce), where is the forward mutation, is the witness program, is the recovery program, and Ce is the declared effect contract. In EvoUndo recovery repair, the forward mutation is strictly immutable (mrepaired m0): m0 is locked at Turn 0 and executed verbatim. Only the witness capture program w, recovery program u, and declared effect contract Ce may be revised across repair turns. The contract is constrained to the runtimes typed effect-contract vocabulary; if omitted, the compiler infers it from the locked forward operations. Although mutable, Ce is not trusted as complete: the runtime independently computes E(m, s) = SnapshotDiff(s, m(s)) ExecutionTraceEffects(m, s) and admission requires E(m, s) Ce. Omitting an observed effect therefore fails the contract audit, whereas overdeclaration enlarges the equivalence scope that recovery must satisfy. The immutability of prevents evasion by weakening the forward mutation to no-op, while independent effect tracking prevents evasion by shrinking the declared recovery scope. 3.2 Counterfactual Round-Trip Verification For each counterfactual state = Qdev Qhid, EvoUndo evaluates the round trip m u(,z) ˆs, checking whether ˆs Ce s. Development states Qdev generate state-level diagnostic feedback. In the original factorial, hidden state contents and per-state outcomes are withheld, although aggregate IID/OOD recovery LCB summaries are returned during repair. The fresh-holdout study instead uses fully feedback-isolated hidden set for final admission. 3.3 Diagnostic Feedback Granularity When development round trip fails, the verifier computes the state residual res = Diff Ce (s, ˆs). Under coarse typed diagnosis (D0), the model receives the affected subsystem and defect classification without exact residual locations. Under exact-address diagnosis (D1), the feedback is enriched with canonical verifier-observed state addresses and ordering traces (prompts in Appendix H). 3.4 Recovery Languages Synthesis is bounded by formal recovery language L. Table 1 gives the implemented primitives and operational semantics. Witness capture runs before m, recording typed pre-state values in w; recovery operations may only reference these captures. L0 covers configuration, prompt, tool-registry, and routing state. L1 extends it with middleware sequences, event listeners, sandboxed files, managed sockets, and ordered composition of recovery operations across surfaces. For example, mutation that prepends middleware and registers listener is recovered by unregistering/restoring the listener before restoring the prior middleware sequence in strict LIFO dependency order. The runtime rejects any L1-only primitive emitted under L0 and consumes that synthesis attempt. These are implemented operational semantics, not completeness characterization of recovery programs. 3.5 Closed-Loop Synthesis and Admission If capability-positive mutation fails recovery verification, EvoUndo initiates bounded synthesis over (w, u, Ce) up to budget {1, 2, 3, 4} with early stopping while keeping m0 fixed. Proposals passing Qdev are evaluated on Qhid. To prevent empirical variance on small sample sizes from admitting unsound mutations, admission requires the 95% Wilson score lower confidence bound LCB0.95(k, n) τR = 0.85, where of hidden counterfactuals pass verification. EvoUndo fails closed: syntax errors, unhandled exceptions, or out-of-language primitives result in immediate rejection, ensuring every admitted state transition satisfies the configured empirical counterfactual recoverability criterion over the modeled harness state.

sections.content: 4.1 Harness State and Task Benchmark The natural benchmark comprises six 100-task architectural families (N = 600): Configuration, Tools, Middleware, Listeners, Resources, and Multi-Surface. Forward capability Jt(m(S)) evaluates postcondition satisfaction for each task independently of recovery syntax. 4.2 Model, Inference, and Verification Protocol Factorial repair and synthesis experiments use the open-weights gpt-oss-120b model under native MXFP4 precision at temperature 0.2 with medium reasoning effort on eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs. In the primary factorial study on the frozen 197-task cohort, each candidate is evaluated across Qdev = 10 development states and Qhid = 40 hidden states (20 IID, 20 OOD). IID states perturb pre-state boundary values, prior-existence states (absent vs. conflicting tool schemas), and combinatorial surface assignments. OOD states introduce true structural shifts: unfamiliar nested keys, conflicting socket allocations, prepended high-priority middleware, multi-level file paths, and reverse routing defaults (detailed taxonomy in Appendix D). Generalization is further verified on an untouched 300-task fresh holdout with 100-state hidden evaluation (Section 7). In separate controlled audit of 300 intentionally incomplete effect contracts across all six harness families, independent dynamic effect tracking detected every injected undeclared semantic effect (300/300), with no false positives on 300 matched complete contracts; Appendix provides details. 4.3 Controlled Benchmark and Natural Failure Bank We construct controlled benchmark of 120 capability-positive mutations with deliberately injected witness/recovery defects across the modeled state types. Next, we construct natural failure bank by sampling one candidate mutation for each of 600 unseen self-evolution tasks without rerolls. Of these, 281 are already admissible, 122 are capability-inadequate, and 197 are capabilitypositive but fail recovery verification. These 197 frozen natural failures constitute our primary evaluation cohort. 4.4 Solvability Audit and Mechanistic Strata To distinguish synthesis search failures from empirical representational limits under the implemented recovery languages, we perform zero-generation constructive oracle audit. Under base language L0, only 48/197 mutations are oracle-recoverable. Under extended language L1, 191/197 are oracle-recoverable. We define empirical oracle recoverability Roracle L,Q (m) {0, 1} as successful recovery synthesis and hidden-state admission by the deterministic constructive oracle under language L. This partitions the failure bank into two disjoint mechanistic strata: S0 = {m : Roracle S1 = {m : Roracle L0,Q (m) = 1}, L1,Q (m) = 1 Roracle S0 = 48, L0,Q (m) = 0}, S1 = 143. (3) (4) Six tasks were not recovered by the deterministic L1 oracle and are excluded from stratum contrasts. The oracle observes the complete pre-state s, the frozen mutation AST m, Ce, and both evaluator suites (10 development and 40 hidden states); this includes privileged state and hiddensuite information unavailable to deployed synthesizer. It is used only for retrospective empirical stratification: no model receives oracle programs, traces, outputs, or hidden per-state outcomes. Across 10 independent resamplings from the implemented counterfactual generator (seeds 1000 10000), membership was unchanged (Jaccard = 1.0000 for S0 and S1; zero migrations across 1,970 task-seed evaluations; Appendix G). This supports stability under the implemented generator, not completeness, distribution-independent task labels, or invariance under arbitrary OOD, adversarial, or structurally different counterfactual generators. 4.5 GroundingExpressivity Factorial and Contrasts We evaluate 2 2 factorial crossing diagnostic granularity with recovery language: {D0, D1} {L0, L1}. Before execution, we protocol-locked three confirmatory paired contrasts: C1: D1L0 vs. D0L0 on S0 (tests exact state-address grounding when L0 is sufficient). C2: D0L1 vs. D0L0 on S1 (tests recovery-language expressivity on the S1 stratum). C3: D1L1 vs. D0L1 on S1 (tests diagnostic grounding on top of an expressive language). We report Rescue@B (fraction of defects repaired within budget B), paired risk differences with 95% bootstrap CIs, and exact two-sided McNemar tests with HolmBonferroni correction. Extended related work is detailed in Appendix A.

sections.title: 5 Controlled and Natural Recovery Results
sections.content: 5.1 Controlled Recoverability: Repair Succeeds When Representation Aligns On the 120-task controlled benchmark, independent regeneration recovers only 4/120 (3.3%) defects at budget = 4. In contrast, closed-loop verifier feedback achieves high repair rates: generic feedback recovers 104/120 (86.7%), raw verifier traces recover 101/120 (84.2%), typed diagnosis recovers 114/120 (95.0%), and prescriptive hints reach 117/120 (97.5%). Thus, when defects fall within the languages representational envelope, closed-loop repair is highly effective. 5.2 Natural Failures Break Conventional Repair On the frozen cohort of 197 natural self-evolution failures, this success collapses entirely. Under the base representation (L0), all four verifier-guided repair modes achieve 0/197 (0.0%) recovery at = 4, while independent regeneration recovers 6/197 (3.0%). Diagnostic analysis reveals that 180/197 natural failures involve structural state transformations outside the predefined controlled defect taxonomy. End-to-end 600-task accounting. Of all 600 unseen tasks, 478/600 (79.67%) produced capability-positive mutations: 281 were already admissible and 197 were recovery-defective. Under D0L1 at = 4, EvoUndo rescues 180/197 (91.37%) defects, yielding 461/478 (96.44%) admissible capability-positive mutations and 461/600 (76.83%) total benchmark yield. Relative to the initially admissible 281/600 (46.83%), this is +30.00 pp absolute increase. Because recovery repair executes the frozen m0 verbatim and revises only (w, u, Ce), all 180 rescued candidates retain their original positive forward capability; zero forward-capability regressions were introduced by recovery repair. This fixed-m0 result does not establish the capabilityrecoverability trade-off under joint optimization with m.

The paired risk difference is = +99.30 pp (95% CI [+97.90, +100.00], pHolm = 1.08 1042). This demonstrates that providing adequate recovery primitives overcomes the expressivity bottleneck, allowing the model to synthesize valid recovery programs for nearly all tasks in S1. 6.3 C3: Diagnostic Specificity Interacts Non-Monotonically with Language Capacity Crucially, adding exact-address feedback on top of the expressive language L1 does not improve performance. On S1, recovery drops from 142/143 (99.3%) under D0L1 to 133/143 (93.0%) under D1L1. The paired risk difference is = 6.29 pp (95% CI [11.19, 2.10], exact McNemar pHolm = 0.0117). Authenticated trace review finds 11 discordant tasks: 10 succeed only under D0L1 (five over-decomposition errors, three sequence inversions, and two over-capture collisions under D1L1), while one succeeds only under D1L1 because the exact address resolves an ambiguous target. The D1L1 failures use fewer raw patch operations and completion tokens than the matched D0L1 successes (means 1.90 vs. 2.80 operations; 626.5 vs. 713.0 tokens). Thus, the negative interaction is not explained by longer generated recoveries; instead, the discordant traces suggest that exact-address feedback changes semantic decomposition and ordering choices. This is descriptive mechanism consistent with the observed traces, not causal intervention; coarse-to-exact diagnostic curricula and constrained address-use strategies were not evaluated (Appendix H). 6.4 Synthesis Efficiency and Interaction Synthesis efficiency η(D, L) = model rescues oracle recoverable separates failures of model synthesis from failures of the recovery representation. The denominator counts only tasks for which the deterministic oracle establishes that the assigned language can express an admissible recovery. Efficiency is therefore 0.0% for D0L0, rises to 79.2% for D1L0, and reaches 94.2% for D0L1. Adding exact-address diagnostics to the rich language lowers efficiency to 87.4%. Thus, once representational feasibility is held fixed, coarse diagnosis with the expressive language realizes the largest fraction of available recoveries. The full-cohort interaction effect on gpt-oss-120b is = (D1L1 D0L1) (D1L0 D0L0) = 25.89 pp (95% CI [34.01, 18.27]). This negative interaction means that exact grounding is highly beneficial when the recovery language is restrictive, but does not provide an additive benefit once richer recovery primitives are available. Instead, on the primary backbone it reduces recovery on S1 by 6.29 pp. The result supports treating diagnostic granularity as modelrepresentation design choice rather than assuming that more specific verifier feedback is uniformly better. 7 Table 3: Cross-model mechanistic contrasts on the frozen 96-task Qwen3.8-27B replication. We independently replicated the factorial on frozen 96-task subset using Qwen3.8-27B with constrained structured decoding; Table 3 summarizes the paired contrasts, while Appendix H.5 reports all factorial cells. The two primary mechanisms transfer: exact-address grounding improves recovery under L0 on S0 by 47.92 pp, and extending the recovery language on S1 improves recovery by 37.50 pp. Both effects remain significant after HolmBonferroni correction. Absolute yields are lower than on gpt-oss-120b, but the direction of both bottleneck-removal effects is preserved. The third contrast qualifies the primary-backbone result. sections.title: 7 Fresh-Holdout Validation and Robustness
sections.content: To verify that L1 does not overfit the 197-task cohort, we evaluated the frozen L1 language across 300 fresh unseen tasks (50 per family) with 100-state hidden evaluation suite (Table 8 in Appendix I). Increasing the number of diverse development counterfactuals from Q2 to Q20 eliminated development-to-hidden false positives (16.8% 0.0%). However, under fixed budget = 4, strict development verification reduced end-to-end yield (Rescue@4100 fell from 49.7% to 35.0%, = 14.67 pp, = 5.76 106), illustrating fundamental precisioncoverage trade-off in counterfactual test design. Sensitivity and Robustness Analysis. Robustness of the recovery framework was comprehensively evaluated across multiple operational dimensions: synthesis budgets {1, 2, 3, 4} (Appendix H), recovery admission thresholds τR {0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90, 0.95}  (Table 10)  , development set configurations (Q2, Q5, Q10, Q20, and Q10-Narrow, Table 8), and hidden sample sizes nhid {10, 20, 30, 50, 100}  (Table 9)  . Across these sweeps, the qualitative behavior of counterfactual verification remains stable: stricter development verification improves precision at the cost of synthesis yield, while admission remains reasonably stable under moderate threshold choices. The grounding and expressivity effects are independently supported by the protocol-locked factorial and cross-model replication. Increasing development set diversity (Q2 Q20) strictly eliminates false positives (16.8% 0.0%) at the cost of expanding the conservatism gap (6.6% 24.1%). Recovery yields remain broadly stable across moderate thresholds τR [0.75, 0.90] (168 to 142 rescues under Q2), but setting stringent threshold of τR = 0.95 materially depresses end-to-end yield (dropping to 102 rescues), indicating that recovery yield is threshold-sensitive at extreme stringencies rather than strictly invariant. Inference and Verification Overhead. Across the 300-task fresh holdout, inference cost ranges from 2.393.09 model calls and approximately 3.37k4.30k generated tokens per task, with higher verification strictness increasing cost (Table 11 in Appendix I). On the primary 197-task factorial cohort, closed-loop repair averaged 1.78 calls/task in D0L1, 1.95 calls/task in D1L1, and 2.40 calls/task in D1L0, with mean model call latencies between 5.25s and 5.85s on H200 GPUs. Detailed fresh-holdout token counts, median latencies, and tokens per successful rescue are reported in Appendix I.

sections.title: 8 Discussion and Limitations
sections.content: Our findings show that self-evolution failures cannot be solved purely by scaling prompting or reasoning effort: without adequate state addresses or recovery primitives, iterative repair fails completely (0/197). Moreover, diagnostic feedback interacts non-monotonically with language expressivity on the primary model. These results argue against treating maximal diagnostic specificity as universally preferable; diagnostic granularity should be treated as modeland representationdependent synthesis parameter. An adaptive diagnostic strategyescalating from coarse failure indicators to granular state traces only when coarse repair failsis plausible mitigation, but no diagnostic curriculum or address-use constraint was evaluated here. Snapshot and transactional recovery. EvoUndo is not intended to dominate effect-scoped snapshots when the complete affected pre-state is known and cheaply serializable. On 300 differentsurface selective-recovery tasks, effect-scoped snapshots recover 300/300 (100.0%) versus 243/300 (81.0%) for EvoUndo; under same-surface concurrency, both degrade to 159/300 (53.0%) and 131/300 (43.7%), respectively. Full snapshots recover 0/300 in both regimes because they clobber subsequent state. Mean storage/latency are 177.8 B/0.039 ms for effect-scoped snapshots, 393.6 B/0.050 ms for EvoUndo, and 1165.0 B/0.084 ms for full snapshots  (Table 5)  . Thus effect-scoped snapshots dominate when exact affected pre-state is known, serializable, and directly restorable; EvoUndo addresses cases where inverse semantics are missing, state-dependent, structured, or must be synthesized. ARIES-style WAL provides transactional rollback when write semantics are predefined (Mohan et al., 1992), but no WAL or ARIES runtime was implemented or evaluated. snapshot/WAL/synthesis hybrid dispatcher is future work. Proof-based verification and runtime enforcement. Astrogator verifies LLM-generated Ansible programs against formal query using symbolic interpretation, providing deductive guarantees within its specified automation calculus (Councilman et al., 2025). EvoUndo instead provides empirical typed round-trip evidence over heterogeneous modeled harness states; this covers recovery properties without claiming proof-level completeness. AgentSpec enforces per-action runtime policies through triggers, predicates, and enforcement actions (Wang et al., 2025); such governance is orthogonal to whether an admitted persistent mutation can later restore prior state, so the two mechanisms can be composed. Limitations and Data Governance: (1) The implemented L0/L1 calculi are specialized to the modeled harness state types and have no formal completeness guarantee; transfer to richer stacks is untested. (2) Repair keeps strictly immutable while allowing only (w, u, Ce) to change; joint optimization with or transactional redesign of was not evaluated. (3) Typed equivalence and effect tracking cover in-memory configuration, prompts, routing, tools, middleware, listeners, virtual sandboxed files, and managed resource handles, but not distributed databases, multi-host state, third-party APIs, unmanaged OS processes, or unmodeled external network state. These settings require additional mechanisms such as distributed observational contracts and transactional protocols. (4) Irreversible physical or financial effects require compensation semantics rather than exact (5) Experiments primarily evaluate gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3.8-27B; broader restoration. model scales remain untested. (6) Production witness capture requires access control, encryption, finite retention, least-privilege schemas, and field-level redaction.

sections.title: 9 Conclusion
sections.content: We introduced EvoUndo, demonstrating that safe self-evolution requires co-designing verification, state grounding, witness semantics, and recovery language expressivity. When recovery representations are aligned, LLMs reliably synthesize state-dependent recovery programs, establishing principled foundation for auditable, self-evolving autonomous agents. AI Use Statement Generative AI tools were used for coding assistance and draft editing. 9 Reproducibility Statement All code, task definitions, counterfactual generators, protocol locks, and evaluation traces will be released openly. Appendix AK provides complete architectural schemas, extended related work, language specifications, prompts, baseline comparisons, and statistical derivations. Ethics Statement This work develops safety constraints for autonomous agents. Experiments run in isolated sandboxes without human subjects or sensitive production data. Deployment in live infrastructure requires additional authorization and audit controls.

sections.title: A Extended Related Work
sections.content: Self-Improving and Self-Evolving Agents. The concept of systems that iteratively modify their own internal behavior dates back to Schmidhubers Godel machine formulation of self-referential improvement (Schmidhuber, 2003). Recent advances in LLMs have made autonomous selfmodification empirically practical. Godel Agent enables an LLM agent to recursively modify its own logic and optimization procedure (Yin et al., 2024), while the Darwin Godel Machine maintains an evolving population of self-modified coding agents and retains modifications according to downstream task performance (Zhang et al., 2026b). More recent work extends self-improvement from model weights or monolithic agent code to the surrounding executable harness. Self-Harness iteratively mines weaknesses, proposes harness modifications, and validates them using held-out performance (Zhang et al., 2026a), while Agentic Harness Engineering uses explicit editable components, trajectory-derived evidence, and outcome validation to evolve coding-agent harnesses (Lin et al., 2026). Recent work further treats the executable harness itself as an optimization target. Retrospective Harness Optimization (RHO) improves an agent harness from prior trajectories using self-validation and self-preference, without requiring an external labeled validation set (Pan et al., 2026). Co-Harness jointly alternates harness optimization with model-parameter optimization, allowing the runtime scaffolding and the underlying model to co-evolve (Chen et al., 2026). Harness-R1 instead learns dedicated harness-engineering policy that converts batches of agent failures into validated executable runtime patches optimized for downstream task success (Shao et al., 2026). Related approaches optimize specific parts of the agent system: Agent symbolic learning treats prompts, tools, and pipeline structure as learnable symbolic parameters and updates them using language-based analogues of optimization (Zhou et al., 2024); EvoTool evolves modular tooluse policies through trajectory-grounded failure attribution, targeted mutation, and population selection (Yang et al., 2026a); and Tool-R0 uses self-play to co-evolve task generation and tool-use capability without an initial supervised task dataset (Acikgoz et al., 2026). Across both holistic harness optimization and component-level methods, existing work optimizes forward utility or policy capability; EvoUndo addresses the complementary question of whether persistent model-generated edits retain independently verified recovery semantics. Reversible Agent Execution and Runtime Effects. Recent agent runtimes have begun treating reversibility as first-class systems property. GoEX develops runtime for autonomous LLM actions centered on post-facto validation, providing undo mechanisms and damage confinement so that executed actions can either be reverted or have their possible impact bounded (Patil et al., 2024). Shepherd represents agentenvironment interactions as typed effects and supports scoped fork, replay, discard, and rollback of reversible execution state (Yu et al., 2026). Related work on spatiotemporal composability formalizes dynamic software components whose effects can be reverted when components are removed, providing foundation for dynamically loadable agent harnesses (Shi et al., 2026). These systems provide runtime mechanisms for reversible or compensable effects. EvoUndo studies distinct challenge that arises when the modification itself is synthesized by an LLM: the required recovery procedure may be unknown, state-dependent, or inexpressible in the available recovery language. We therefore treat witness capture and recovery synthesis as objects of verification rather than assuming that correct inverse semantics are supplied by the component author or runtime. Reversible Programming and Bidirectional State Transformation. Reversible computation and bidirectional programming study transformations for which information required to reconstruct prior states is preserved or explicitly represented. Reversible-effect systems extend these ideas to stateful computations and mutable effects (Heunen et al., 2018). Classical bidirectional transformations, particularly lenses, formalize paired transformations that propagate updates between related state representations while satisfying consistency laws (Foster et al., 2007). EvoUndo shares the need to retain sufficient prior-state information for reverse state transformation, but differs because its forward edits and recovery programs are model-generated, and recovery correctness is evaluated empirically across counterfactual harness states. Consequently, non-injective forward mutation 12 need not be rejected when state-dependent witness preserves the information required for recovery. Verification of Agent Modifications. Self-improving agents commonly validate candidate modifications through downstream benchmarks, regression tests, or deterministic evaluation, including population-based self-modification (Zhang et al., 2026b) and harness optimization (Zhang et al., 2026a; Lin et al., 2026). Such validation can determine whether modification improves capability without establishing whether its persistent effects can be removed. EvoUndo separates these properties: forward capability is evaluated through the task objective, while recovery is independently evaluated through counterfactual round trips; development states provide diagnostics, while hidden-state contents and per-state outcomes are withheld. In the primary factorial, aggregate hidden IID/OOD LCB summaries are nevertheless returned during repair. This distinction is central: mutation may improve task performance and pass ordinary regression tests while still destroying information, leaking state, or requiring recovery operations unavailable in the current representation. Formal Verification of Self-Evolving Agents. SEVerA studies self-evolving agent synthesis under formal correctness constraints, using formally guarded generative-model calls and program verification to ensure that synthesized agents satisfy specified contracts independently of learned model parameters (Banerjee et al., 2026). This provides stronger deductive guarantees than EvoUndos empirical counterfactual verification. The two approaches address complementary properties: SEVerA verifies that generated agent programs satisfy formal behavioral constraints, whereas EvoUndo asks whether persistent, model-generated harness mutations can be returned to their prior observational state using state-dependent witness and recovery semantics. Runtime Safety Enforcement. AARM treats agent action execution as security boundary and proposes runtime control layer that intercepts actions before execution, evaluates them against authorization and intent policies, and records execution evidence (Errico, 2026). AgentSpec similarly introduces lightweight domain-specific language for specifying and enforcing runtime safety constraints on LLM agents through explicit triggers, predicates, and enforcement actions (Wang et al., 2025). VIGIL similarly converts behavioral specifications into executable runtime policies over agenttool traces, including temporal, argument, and value-flow constraints (Li et al., 2026). Such systems determine whether an action sequence satisfies behavioral policy; EvoUndo targets different temporal property: whether persistent harness self-modification can later be removed while restoring the relevant prior harness state. Runtime policy enforcement and recoverabilityconstrained evolution can therefore be composed. Persistent self-evolution also creates security risks beyond per-action authorization: Zombie Agents demonstrates that attacker-controlled content can be incorporated into an agents evolving long-term memory and persist across sessions, later inducing unauthorized behavior (Yang et al., 2026b). EvoUndo studies whether persistent harness modifications carry recovery semantics that permit their effects to be independently verified and removed.

sections.title: B EvoUndo Implementation Details
sections.content: B.1 Harness State Representation We represent the agent harness as typed persistent state containing configuration, prompt templates, routing state, tool registries, middleware sequences, event-listener bindings, sandboxed files, and managed resources. Each state target is associated with canonical addressing scheme and type-specific observational equivalence policy. B.2 Candidate Representation Each EvoUndo candidate is represented as ξ = (m, w, u, Ce), where is the frozen forward mutation, is the witness-capture program, is the recovery program, and Ce is the effect contract. In EvoUndo recovery repair, the forward mutation is strictly immutable (mrepaired m0). Only the witness capture program w, recovery program u, and declared effect contract Ce may be revised across repair turns. The contract is constrained to the runtimes typed effect-contract 13 vocabulary; when omitted, it is inferred from the locked forward operations. The runtime independently computes E(m, s) = SnapshotDiff(s, m(s)) ExecutionTraceEffects(m, s) and requires E(m, s) Ce: an omitted observed effect causes rejection, while over-declaration expands the state scope that must satisfy recovery equivalence. B.3 Canonical State Addresses object identities. Verifier diagnostics use canonical semantic state locations rather than raw implementationinclude tools["tool id"], specific config["key"], and resources["resource id"]. Canonicalization is applied uniformly across verifier residual extraction and diagnostic rendering. Diagnostic addresses exposed to the recovery model are derived only from verifier-visible development executions. middleware["middleware id"], files["path"],

sections.title: C Recovery Languages
sections.content: C.1 Base Recovery Language L0 The original recovery language supports local operations for configuration, prompt, tool-registry, and routing state. Its implemented capture, forward, and recovery primitives are enumerated in Table 1. The L0 runtime explicitly rejects operations requiring middleware-sequence, listener, fileprestate, socket-descriptor, or ordered multi-surface semantics. C.2 Extended Recovery Language L1 L1 strictly extends L0 with five implemented capability classes identified by the natural-failure solvability audit: 1. Indexed sequence capture and restoration: preserves both sequence membership and ordering information. 2. Listener capture and restoration: records the prior event binding and restores it OpSpec(op type="restore listener", target="<event name>", listener with with witness key="<w key>") removes OpSpec(op type="unregister listener", target="<event name>"). registered newly or 3. File pre-state capture and restoration: captures whether file existed and, when necessary, its previous contents or state. 4. Resource-descriptor capture and restoration: preserves state required to restore resourcebacked effects. 5. Ordered multi-surface recovery: permits recovery of interacting state mutations in an explicitly specified order. The runtime enforces the requested language level. An L1-only primitive emitted in an L0 condition is classified as an invalid model output and consumes the corresponding synthesis attempt. These are implemented operational semantics and do not establish formal language completeness.

The effect contract Ce determines which state targets and semantic properties are relevant for candidate. For configuration entries, equivalence requires restoration of the relevant key and value state. Tool and registry-like state requires restoration of the relevant binding, including the registered identity and associated implementation state represented by the harness. Middleware and other sequence-like state requires both membership and ordering to match the pre-mutation state. Listener state requires restoration of the relevant registration state. File-backed effects require restoration of the relevant pre-state, including existence and file state when represented by the recovery contract. Resource-backed effects require restoration of the relevant descriptor and lifecycle state represented by the harness. For compound mutations touching multiple state targets, every contract-relevant target must satisfy its corresponding equivalence policy. The verifier compares only properties represented by the typed harness state and declared observational contract rather than requiring raw object-identity equality. D.3 Effect-Contract Coverage Audit to evaluate whether dynamic effect We conducted controlled audit tracking reliably detects undeclared side effects. The runtime constructs E(m, s) = SnapshotDiff(s, m(s)) ExecutionTraceEffects(m, s) and requires E(m, s) Ce; any observed effect omitted from the declared contract therefore causes rejection. For 300 mutations spanning all six harness families, we constructed intentionally incomplete effect contracts by omitting at least one ground-truth affected target Etrue. Dynamic effect tracking detected every injected undeclared semantic effect (300/300, 100.0%), with zero false positives across 300 matched complete contracts (0/300, 0.0%). In an additional 300 nondeterministic runtime controls (varying OS thread IDs, timestamps, and memory pointer representations), the canonicalizer produced zero false alarms. These guarantees apply to the modeled harness state space and do not extend to unmodeled external OS processes or out-of-band network state. D.4 Snapshot-Restore Baselines To compare EvoUndo against direct runtime snapshotting, we evaluated full-state snapshots and effect-scoped snapshots across = 300 tasks under two multi-step mutation regimes: (1) Differentsurface selective recovery, where subsequent mutations modify disjoint harness surfaces; and (2) Same-surface concurrent recovery, where subsequent mutations modify the same structured surface. sections.title: E Controlled Recoverability Benchmark
sections.content: The controlled benchmark contains 120 deliberately recovery-defective but capability-positive candidates. The forward mutation is held fixed and the defective recovery specification is produced by corrupting witness or recovery semantics. The benchmark includes missing witness capture, dummy witness capture, incorrect recovery operations, resource leakage, and hidden-effect omission. Every benchmark item has known recoverable counterpart under the available recovery representation, allowing the experiment to isolate recovery synthesis from language expressivity. At budget = 4, the principal recovery results are: Strict regeneration: 4/120 (3.3%) Generic feedback: 104/120 (86.7%) Raw verifier traces: 101/120 (84.2%) Typed diagnosis: 114/120 (95.0%) Prescriptive guidance: 117/120 (97.5%)

sections.title: F Natural Failure Bank
sections.content: We construct the natural-failure population by generating one candidate mutation for each of 600 unseen self-evolution tasks with no rerolls, using the six 100-task benchmark families defined in Section 4. The resulting population is: 281/600 already admissible, 197/600 capability-positive but recovery-defective, 122/600 capability inadequate. The 197 recovery-defective candidates are frozen before subsequent repair, solvability, and factorial analyses. Under the original recovery representation, Generic, Raw, Typed, and Prescriptive repair each recover 0/197 natural failures at budget = 4. Strict regeneration recovers 6/197.

sections.title: G Oracle Solvability Audit Methodology and Robustness
sections.content: To distinguish synthesis search failures from empirical representational limitations under the implemented recovery languages, we conducted zero-generation constructive oracle solvability audit across all 197 frozen natural recovery failures. 16 G.1 Deterministic Constructive Principles The solvability oracle is fully deterministic and non-generative. Specifically: No LLM calls: The oracle contains no stochastic generation or learned model inference. No search or enumeration: Recovery programs are constructed directly via deterministic structural compilation rather than heuristic search, beam search, or candidate enumeration. No retries or task heuristics: Every candidate undergoes single-pass deterministic transformation with zero task-specific manual tuning. Disclaimer: This is empirical recoverability under the implemented deterministic constructive oracle, not formal proof of language-theoretic completeness. G.2 Oracle Inputs and Construction Algorithm The constructive oracle takes four formal inputs: 1. The frozen forward mutation abstract syntax tree (AST) m. 2. The pre-mutation harness state s. 3. The declared effect contract Ce. 4. The evaluator state distributions Qdev (Qdev = 10) and Qhid (Qhid = 40). For each forward operation fi m: 1. Witness Construction: The oracle deterministically constructs witness capture operation wi that queries and stores the pre-mutation state of the targeted surface address. 2. Inverse Construction: The oracle deterministically constructs the corresponding inverse recovery primitive ui permitted under the target language grammar L. 3. LIFO Unwinding Execution: The synthesized recovery program orders inverse operations in exact reverse (Last-In, First-Out) order: = (uk, . . . , u1). G.3 Language Expressivity Boundaries Base Recovery Language L0. Supports the implemented configuration, prompt, tool-registry, and routing primitives enumerated in Table 1. It strictly prohibits middleware-sequence, listener, fileprestate, socket-descriptor, and ordered multi-surface operations. Extended Recovery Language L1. Extends L0 with: 1. Indexed Sequence Restoration: Preserves sequence membership, element identity, and exact insertion index for ordered lists (e.g., middleware chains). 2. Listener Capture and Restoration: Uses restore listener or unregister listener for surface. capture listener with the distinct event-listener 3. File Pre-State Preservation: Captures pre-existence status and SHA-256 validated content buffers. 4. Resource Descriptor Management: Captures managed socket descriptors for restoration or release. 5. Ordered Multi-Surface Unwinding: Executes the implemented recovery operations in explicit reverse-dependency order. G.4 Admission Criterion for Oracle Solvability mutation is classified as empirically recoverable under language if and only if: 1. The synthesized (w, u) candidate compiles strictly within the language gate for L. 2. Forward capability is preserved: J(m; S) > 0. 3. Round-trip verification achieves 10/10 (100.0%) on development states Qdev. 4. The 95% Wilson score lower confidence bound satisfies LCB0.95 τR = 0.85 over the hidden states Qhid. 5. Recovered states pass identical typed observational equivalence ˆs Ce s. G.5 Representative Authenticated Case Studies Case A: Configuration in S0 (nat cfg 012 max retries). The forward mutation executes set config("max retries", 5). The deterministic constructive oracle records the pre-mutation scalar value with capture config and constructs the corresponding restore config recovery operation using that witness. This candidate compiles and satisfies full round-trip equivalence under both L0 and L1. registers Case B: Tool Registration tation (nat tool 004 003 dependency grapher). the with unregister tool("tool 003 dependency grapher"). registration is supported in the base grammar, the recovery compiles and succeeds under L0. forward mutool 003 dependency grapher records constructs Because single-tool un- (nat tool 004 003). Reversing this sequence mutation requires the indexed capture middleware and restore middleware operations. Under L0, these operations are outside the grammar and rejected by the language gate. Under L1, the oracle constructs the valid sequence restoration program, achieving 100% recovery on hidden counterfactuals. (nat mw 001 000). The the middleware S1 limiter into Case D: Multi-Surface Task in S1 (nat multi 036 mw and event). The forward mutation registers an event callback listener and prepends an audit logger to the middleware stack. Under L0, recovery fails because multi-surface coordination is outside the L0 grammar. Under L1, the oracle constructs an ordered LIFO unwind program using unregister listener before restore middleware, satisfying the observational contract Ce across all 40 hidden states. G.6 Oracle Stratum Resampling Stability Sweep To evaluate whether the empirical strata S0 and S1 are sensitive to the specific counterfactual prestates sampled in Qdev and Qhid, we re-evaluated the deterministic constructive oracle across 10 independently resampled counterfactual seeds (seeds 1000 through 10000) using the same generative state distribution. distinct counterfactual suite was generated for each seed. Across all 10 independent resamplings, stratum membership was unchanged (S0 = 48, S1 = 143, unrecovered = 6, Jaccard = 1.0000 for both S0 and S1, with zero stratum migrations across 1,970 task-seed evaluations). This establishes empirical stability under independent resampling from the implemented generator; it does not establish completeness, distribution-independent task labels, or invariance under arbitrary OOD, adversarial, or structurally different counterfactual generators.

sections.title: H Factorial Protocol and Additional Results
sections.content: H.1 Diagnostic Prompt and Model-Call Configuration The system prompt is identical in all four factorial cells: 18 You are an expert self-evolving agent compiler generating verified repairs. Under D0, each repair call receives the following diagnostic fields: Verification Result: RECOVERY_EQUIVALENCE_FAILED Affected Subsystems: <task.surfaces> Defect Summary: The candidate executed forward mutations on <task.surfaces> without registering complete, sound inverse capture and recovery operations. Dev Recovery Rate: <dev_recovery_rate * 100>% (Required: 100.0%) Hidden IID LCB: <hidden_iid_lcb> (Required: >= 0.85) Hidden OOD LCB: <hidden_ood_lcb> (Required: >= 0.85) The D1 condition uses the same diagnostic content and additionally appends the exact-address diagnostic bundle: Diagnostic Mode: D1_EXACT_ADDRESS Forward Effect Order: <forward_effect_order> Observed State Residuals: <observed_state_residuals> Residual Count: <residual_count> Verifier Observation: <diagnostic_evidence> All four factorial cells use the same model-call configuration: openai/gpt-oss-120b at the frozen experimental revision, temperature 0.2, medium reasoning effort, and an explicit maximum of 2,048 generated tokens per call. The models native 131,072-token context window is available without additional input truncation. H.2 Budgeted Recovery Progression For the final strict-L0 D1L0 execution, cumulative rescue progresses as follows: 24/197 at = 1, 35/197 at = 2, 37/197 at = 3, and 38/197 at = 4. All 38 successes belong to S0; no S1 task or task unrecovered by the L1 oracle passes under strict L0. H.3 Language-Gate Behavior Recovery-language assignments are enforced before execution. For each generated recovery program, the runtime gate checks every proposed primitive against the operation set authorized by the assigned language. Under an L0 condition, primitives requiring indexed sequence restoration, listener restoration or unregistration, file pre-state restoration, socket-descriptor restoration, or ordered multi-surface recovery are L1-only and are therefore rejected rather than executed. An outof-language proposal consumes the corresponding synthesis attempt. Across 691 recorded model responses in D1L0, 290 attempted at least one L1-only recovery primitive and were rejected by the language gate: 21/144 (14.6%) on S0 versus 253/523 (48.4%) on S1. The remaining 16 rejections occurred on the six tasks outside the oracle-defined S0/S1 strata. H.4 Discordant Trace Analysis (D1L1 vs. D0L1) We analyzed the 11 discordant tasks between D0L1 and D1L1 on stratum S1 (10 D0L1-only successes and 1 D1L1-only success). Table 6 reports the failure taxonomy alongside quantitative trace metrics extracted from authenticated execution logs. H.5 Cross-Model Replication with Qwen3.8-27B (Step 24B) To evaluate whether the observed grounding and expressivity mechanisms generalize across model architectures, we conducted an independent cross-model replication on Qwen3.8-27B under constrained structured decoding, using the original gpt-oss-120b experiment as historical reference. The replication was conducted on frozen 96-task subset (48 tasks from S0 and 48 tasks from S1). sections.content: For the three protocol-locked contrasts, we use paired two-sided exact McNemar tests. Let and denote discordant pair counts. The exact test uses Binomial(b + c, 0.5) and = 2 Pr [X min(b, c)], capped at one. HolmBonferroni correction is applied jointly across C1, C2, C3. Paired risk-difference confidence intervals are estimated with 100,000 paired bootstrap resamples. sections.title: K Robustness Analysis and Execution Integrity
sections.content: K.1 Family-Level Leave-One-Out Sensitivity Leave-one-family-out estimates remain strongly positive for C1 and C2. For C3, the estimated risk difference remains negative across all leave-one-family-out partitions. The exploratory full-cohort factorial interaction retains its negative sign (I = 25.89 pp, 95% CI [34.01, 18.27]). K.2 Execution Integrity and Protocol Locking The experimental implementation uses fail-closed execution. Model-service failures abort execution, malformed outputs consume an attempt, and recovery primitives outside the assigned language are rejected before execution. Result artifacts, task manifests, protocol configurations, success vectors, and analysis scripts are stored with cryptographic hashes to distinguish authenticated results from superseded runs.
